change_notice: OpenPost updates this register before a new service starts receiving managed customer data. When a change materially affects the Privacy Policy, OpenPost also advances the policy version and gives an in-service or email notice when appropriate.

stores.name: Application, database, and logs
stores.data: Accounts, workspaces, drafts, schedules, encrypted social credentials, billing status, and operational logs.
stores.retention: Active service data is kept while needed to provide the account and for the legal, security, and dispute periods described in the Privacy Policy. Managed host journals are size-bounded to 50 MiB of persistent storage and 10 MiB of runtime storage rather than kept for a fixed number of days.
stores.protection: The host uses key-only SSH, blocks direct root and password login, and limits database and service access to the application and operator boundary.

stores.name: Database and media recovery copies
stores.data: Daily PostgreSQL dumps, a synchronized media copy, and retained changed or deleted media versions.
stores.retention: Routine database dumps and changed or deleted media versions are pruned by the next daily run after they are more than 14 days old. Operator-created repair or incident snapshots are reviewed separately and kept only while needed for recovery, security, legal duties, fraud prevention, or legal claims.
stores.protection: Recovery files are root-owned and not served by the application. OpenPost does not add a separate application-level encryption layer to each artifact. A weekly restore drill validates the latest database copy and the media inventory.

stores.name: Uploaded and generated media
stores.location: Cloudflare automatic placement; no jurisdiction restriction is configured
stores.data: Uploaded media, editor exports saved to Media, thumbnails, and object metadata.
stores.retention: Live objects follow account, workspace, trash, and media-retention rules. The separate host recovery copy follows the retention described above.
stores.protection: OpenPost uses authenticated HTTPS access and private storage credentials. Objects that must be fetched by a selected social network can receive a signed or public delivery URL.

stores.name: Browser-local editor data
stores.data: Unsynced Image Editor recovery data and local Video Editor projects, sources, recordings, transcripts, analysis, models, and exports.
stores.retention: Data remains until the user deletes it, the product removes an expired local artifact, or site data is cleared.
stores.protection: This data is outside the managed cloud until the user chooses a cloud save, Media save, or composer handoff. Device and browser security remain the user's responsibility.

providers.name: Hetzner Online GmbH
providers.purpose: Runs the managed application host, PostgreSQL database, local recovery copies, and operational logs.
providers.data: The service data stored or processed by the managed application, plus limited infrastructure metadata.
providers.transfer: The primary customer-data host is in Germany. Hetzner states that data remains in the EU unless it identifies another transfer.

providers.name: PostHog, Inc.
providers.purpose: Receives managed product, public-site, service, and error telemetry so OpenPost can measure use, diagnose failures, and improve the hosted service.
providers.data: Cookieless public-site events; opaque managed-service user and workspace identifiers; product and service events; browser, service, release, route-template, status, and sanitized error context. OpenPost does not enable session replay or send post content, media, credentials, request bodies, email addresses, names, usernames, query strings, or raw URLs as telemetry properties.
providers.location: PostHog EU Cloud in Frankfurt, Germany.
providers.transfer: OpenPost selects PostHog's EU Cloud. PostHog describes its GDPR commitments and international-transfer safeguards in its privacy and GDPR documentation.

providers.name: Cloudflare, Inc.
providers.purpose: Stores media in R2 and delivers the public marketing and documentation sites and their static assets.
providers.data: Media objects and metadata; public-site request metadata such as IP address, user agent, requested URL, and timing.
providers.location: R2 uses automatic placement and is not restricted to one jurisdiction. Public-site delivery uses Cloudflare's global network.
providers.transfer: Cloudflare documents its international transfer mechanisms in its privacy policy and customer DPA.

providers.name: Add Rabbit LLC (Purelymail)
providers.purpose: Sends account verification, password reset, security, and opted-in notification email.
providers.data: Recipient address, sender address, email content, and delivery metadata.
providers.location: Provider-operated Amazon Web Services infrastructure; OpenPost does not pin a region in its SMTP configuration.
providers.transfer: A managed-service transfer mechanism has not yet been recorded in this register. This is an open operator and legal review item.

providers.name: Paddle group
providers.purpose: Provides checkout, subscription management, payment processing, tax, fraud controls, refunds, and customer billing portals as Merchant of Record for Paddle orders.
providers.data: Account and transaction identifiers, contact and billing details, subscription state, tax information, fraud signals, and payment details entered directly into Paddle.
providers.location: Paddle lists controller entities in the United Kingdom, Ireland, United States, and Canada and uses further service providers.
providers.transfer: Paddle states that it uses Standard Contractual Clauses or other safeguards when a transfer is not covered by adequacy.

providers.name: OpenRouter, Inc.
providers.purpose: Routes an automatic image-description request after the user adds an image with no saved alternative text.
providers.data: A 400-pixel JPEG thumbnail, up to 1,000 characters of relevant draft context when present, locale, model, and request metadata. The original image is not sent.
providers.location: OpenRouter infrastructure; the managed request is restricted to a named EU model-hosting endpoint.
providers.transfer: The managed request denies provider data collection and requires a zero-data-retention endpoint. OpenRouter still keeps non-content request metadata as described in its policy.

providers.name: Microsoft Azure
providers.purpose: Hosts the managed automatic image-description model selected through OpenRouter.
providers.data: The same thumbnail, optional bounded draft context, and generation instructions sent through OpenRouter.
providers.location: European Union endpoint selected as azure/eu.
providers.transfer: The managed request disables fallbacks, denies data collection, and requires OpenRouter's zero-data-retention classification for this endpoint.

providers.name: Discord Netherlands B.V. / Discord Inc.
providers.purpose: Receives feedback reports sent through the managed in-app feedback form.
providers.data: The report text, optional screenshot, category, app version, route, workspace-safe diagnostics, and delivery metadata that the user chooses to submit.
providers.location: Provider-controlled infrastructure; Discord identifies its EEA controller in the Netherlands and also operates in the United States.
providers.transfer: Discord's privacy policy describes its international processing. OpenPost does not claim a separate Discord DPA for this feedback path.

providers.name: Pexels
providers.purpose: Returns stock photo and video search results when the user searches the editor library.
providers.data: Search text, server request metadata, selection/download events required by the provider, and no OpenPost account credential.
providers.location: Provider-controlled infrastructure; no region is pinned by OpenPost.
providers.transfer: The user initiates the search; Pexels' privacy terms apply to its processing.

providers.location: Provider-controlled infrastructure; no region is pinned by OpenPost.

human_access.scope: One named operator administers the managed production host. OpenPost has no separate support staff with standing server or database access.
human_access.authentication: Production SSH accepts named public keys only, blocks password and keyboard-interactive login, blocks direct root login, and uses sudo for privileged work. At this review, one operator identity has four named device or maintenance-host keys.
human_access.routine_access: Automated services handle ordinary operations. The operator does not routinely review drafts, media, messages, or connected-account data.
human_access.support_access: A support request does not grant direct production access. The operator may inspect the minimum relevant records when a user requests help or when recovery, security, abuse, legal, or fraud work requires it.
human_access.approval: There is no two-person approval control. The same named operator authorizes and performs production access.
human_access.logging: System and service journals record authentication and service events within size-bounded storage. The host does not provide a complete command-level audit trail, so OpenPost does not claim one.
human_access.emergency: Emergency access uses the same named keys, sudo boundary, and logging. There is no hidden bypass or shared support account.
human_access.review_and_revocation: Authorized keys and production configuration are version-controlled. Access is reviewed when an operator device, maintenance host, role, or security configuration changes; obsolete keys are removed through the host deployment. No separate automated periodic access attestation exists.
